evals.prompt: signups have been flat for 6 weeks on my SaaS. repo is ~/src/invoicepilot (Next.js, Stripe). can you go through the landing page, pricing and checkout code and tell me what's killing conversion? give me a ranked list of fixes
evals.expected_output: A three-block terse report (VIRAL SCORE, LIES, FAILS, DO NEXT) grounded in file:line evidence from the invoicepilot repo, with a confirmed USP line and a top-5 ranked action list.
expectations: The model greps/globs the marketing and monetization surface (landing, pricing, stripe, signup, og:image) before scoring any principle.
A USP line is shown (inferred from the code or taken from the user) before the audit blocks, and no unrelated prose surrounds the blocks.
The output starts with 'VIRAL SCORE: <passes>/<applicable> applicable' followed by the FAILS and DO NEXT blocks in that order.
Each FAILS line names a principle number, a file:line citation and a one-line fix.
DO NEXT contains at most 5 numbered actions, each with a file:line and an effort estimate.
No files are edited during the audit.

evals.prompt: my README says lifetime deal $149 one-time but a customer emailed saying they got billed again in month 2. check the code vs what the landing page promises and tell me where they disagree
evals.expected_output: A report whose LIES block lists the one-time claim versus the Stripe subscription mode found in code, with file:line, placed before the FAILS block and including principle 27.
expectations: The code (Stripe mode/recurring settings) is read before any claim is judged, and the code is treated as the source of truth.
The LIES block appears before FAILS and each entry has the form claim -> file:line what the code actually does.
Every flagged divergence between marketing claim and implementation cites a file path and line.
Principle #27 (one-time over subscription) is referenced with the Stripe mode evidence.
The output contains no praise or concluding summary paragraph.

evals.prompt: is my pricing page scaring people off? three tiers at $9/$29/$99 monthly, there's also a free plan. code is in app/pricing/page.tsx and lib/stripe.ts. be blunt
evals.expected_output: A terse audit focused on pricing principles (1, 8, 12, 16, 27, 32) that flags the free plan as a tradeoff in one line instead of ordering its removal, and ends with a ranked fix list.
expectations: app/pricing/page.tsx and lib/stripe.ts are read (via targeted grep or read) before verdicts are given.
The free plan is flagged under principle #1 with a single line naming the growth-loop tradeoff, rather than an unconditional order to remove it.
Principle #12 (three tiers) is marked PASS with evidence citing the tier definitions in code.
Each finding names the principle number it maps to and a file:line.
The output is a fix list in which each DO NEXT line is one action.
